parallel.requirements: Recognized the Rust 2021, std-only, black-box, CLI parity, byte-identical output, Cargo project, library module, root test1.rs, and executable requirements.

parallel.implementation: Only /output/Cargo.toml was written by the parent. The workflow design children did not return usable designs, and the judge/spec child remained in failed prototype work rather than producing deliverable Rust files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the prompt requirements and even built a detailed reference matrix for C++ behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt requirements and probed CLI edge cases before implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was broadly comparable; the outcome difference came from execution and delivery, not from missing top-level task knowledge.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed work into a workflow with design, judge, implementation, integration, verification, repair, and final phases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor for the full implementation and verification path with delegation disabled and no subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit owners but depended on child completion; serial kept ownership local and completed the whole pipeline.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied detailed child contracts with fixed paths, root test1.rs, module APIs, and verification requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial internalized those interfaces by writing coherent Cargo, entry, cli, library, and hopscotch module files itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel contracts were not the weak point; they never yielded completed child artifacts for integration, while serial maintained one coherent interface context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote Cargo.toml, created reference tooling, and had a judge child prototype that OOM-killed before a repair tool call was rejected.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all implementation files, including root test1.rs, cli parsing, hopscotch map, iterators, and tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel never delivered the requested Rust implementation; serial did and corrected compile issues along the way.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow design children failed after retries and no parent-level takeover or replacement implementation occurred before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; the same actor wrote, inspected, fixed, and verified the files directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the needed child-result transition from delegation to implementation; serial avoided that dependency and completed local work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel planned disjoint per-file implementers and an integration phase, but the final artifact contained no implementation files to integrate.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated the written files into a Cargo project that artifact validation accepted with test1.rs and src modules present.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no evidence of a write collision; the concrete difference is that parallel produced no assembled final tree while serial did.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified a reference harness against the C++ binary but lacked a Rust artifact for cargo, rustc, or differential acceptance gates.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran cargo build/test, rustc rebuild, 28-case differential testing, byte-level comparison, fuzzing, dependency checks, and final clean build checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial closed the loop against the actual deliverable; parallel only prepared verification infrastructure and then failed official evaluation due missing files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran for the full 2400-second budget, returned 143, and the workflow state ended killed after repeated child stalls.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed normally in 628.27 seconds with return code 0 and remaining provider budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was dominated by unrecovered workflow failure and timeout; serial finished with time left after implementing and verifying.

outcome_analysis.explanation: This is a serial_only_pass outcome. Parallel knew the task and prepared useful probes, but delegated the required implementation behind a workflow whose design children failed after retries and were not taken over before timeout. Consequently the submitted artifact contained only Cargo.toml and missed test1.rs. Serial kept the whole pipeline in one trajectory, wrote the entry and library modules, verified them, and the official evaluator passed all 39 tests.
parallel_contributors: Workflow-dependent design phase failed after repeated child stalls or interruptions and was not taken over by the parent.
The implementation, integration, and final verification phases never produced the required /output/test1.rs or library files.
Artifact validation copied only Cargo.toml, so the completed evaluator had no runnable Rust solution and passed 0/39.
serial_contributors: Single actor retained ownership of probing, writing, compile fixes, integration, and verification.
Serial produced the root test1.rs, Cargo.toml, and all src modules before closure.
Serial verified cargo build/test, rustc build, differential behavior, byte equality, and fuzz cases before final output.
ordinary_implementation_differences: No independent delivered-code defect explains the parallel failure because the parallel implementation files were absent; the judge prototype OOM remained inside an uncompleted child path.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: directly evidenced contributor, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The workflow explicitly assigned implementation to seven per-file implementers after design and judge phases; the failure was not absence of an implementation owner but failure before takeover.
The workflow script explicitly assigned an Integrate phase and integrator role; no completed component set reached integration, so integration was not ownerless.
The workflow planned final assembly and deliverable checks through integration/final phases, but those phases were never reached with usable files.
The workflow itself owned the end-to-end pipeline across design, implementation, integration, verification, repair, and final; it failed after child failures rather than lacking a pipeline owner.
The setup was not a single mandatory preflight or oracle step; the directly evidenced issue is failed design children with no takeover.
The design investigation did not complete as a separate first phase and then squeeze implementation; it repeatedly failed before producing usable designs.
Implementation was left unfinished, but the record points to failed required child work and absent takeover rather than capacity diverted from an active critical path.
Many design retries consumed time, but this is the same stalled-child/no-takeover chain; breadth and timeout are downstream symptoms, not an independent allocation episode.
The design and judge briefs were broad, but no single child assignment is the proven independent cause; repeated child failure and absent takeover better capture the episode.
The workflow child briefs included task, environment, CLI, artifact, black-box, API, and verification requirements; children were not missing a known requirement.
The workflow script pinned file paths and public APIs for separately owned modules; no incompatible independently produced components reached integration.
No known requirement or finding is shown disappearing between actors; the failed children did not produce useful handoffs to lose.
There was no oversized completed handoff that the parent failed to reduce; the key design outputs never returned.
No actor consumed an obsolete result or superseded workspace state; the run stalled before such a handoff decision.
No incompatible completed reports or contracts reached a decision point because design outputs did not return.
The parallel parent did not make an observable whole-task completion claim or accept a partial artifact as complete; it timed out with an empty final response.
The design retries reused similar briefs, but prior attempts produced no reusable checkpoint or confirmed finding; retaining it would duplicate the same stalled-child failure chain.

No implementation result was merged after verification; the workflow did not reach a completed integration/verification sequence.
No delegated implementation completed or became retrievable for the parent to join; implementer phases were not reached with files.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; the workflow never reached a meaningful verification phase.

candidates.near_match_reason: The repeated design retries consumed the time budget, but they are not a separate allocation episode from the failed-child/no-takeover chain.

candidates.reason: There was no completed child result available to the parent and then ignored; the necessary outputs were missing or failed.

No multiple agents wrote competing component files; only Cargo.toml reached the final artifact.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source file with a reconciliation conflict.
No child or parent replaced a non-entry source file produced by another actor.

No broad cleanup or promotion replaced multiple current outputs in the final workspace.
Although workflow children shared /output, the evidence shows no unstable provenance or shared-write conflict; the issue was missing output after child failure.
No generated fixture, temporary artifact, cache, or tool output from one actor was consumed by another as a contaminated reference.

retained_patterns.reason: Required workflow children failed or were cancelled before returning designs/spec work, and the parent did not resume, reassign, or directly complete the implementation before the run closed.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Parallel left the required Rust project unimplemented: artifact validation saw only Cargo.toml, missing test1.rs, and the official evaluation passed 0/39.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Retry fan-out and timeout are visible, but they are downstream of the same failed-child/no-takeover boundary and do not form a separate retained episode.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Early Child Termination, Blind Timeout Wait, Checkpoint-Free Retry, Late Finalization, and Missing Implementation Join were considered but suppressed as the same workflow failure/no-takeover chain or absent completed artifacts.
